paper.title: AgentNet: Decentralized Evolutionary Coordination for LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
paper.central_claim: A decentralized, RAG-memory-based DAG network of LLM agents with no central orchestrator in which agents autonomously specialise (capability vectors, retrieval memory pools), rewire connections (weighted edges, pruning) and route tasks, outperforming centralized multi-agent systems in efficiency, adaptability and scalability and enabling privacy-preserving cross-organisation collaboration.

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref not exposed to the worker by the claude-kimi dispatch; model_type is the configured slot only.

evidence.quote: Each agent maintains a limited-capacity pool of successful task trajectories; when a new task arises, it retrieves the most relevant trajectories through few-shot learning, thus improving decision-making.
evidence.support_explanation: Write rule: only successful trajectory fragments (observation, partial context, action) from steps where the agent took part are stored per router and per executor; read path is embedding top-k retrieval into the prompt. What counts as 'successful' during the training phase is not defined.

evidence.quote: Several factors influence the decision-making process, including the frequency of use, recency of tasks, and the uniqueness of the trajectory. The agent assesses these factors through a prompt-based reasoning process that helps determine the utility of each trajectory.
evidence.support_explanation: Eviction at capacity is decided by an LLM prompt over frequency, recency, uniqueness; no measured utility, counterfactual test or rollback.

evidence.quote: This adaptive weighting mechanism ensures that the network continuously refines its structure based on operational experience.
evidence.support_explanation: Edge weights are updated by an exponential average of a success metric S per routed pair, and edges under threshold theta_w are pruned (Eq. 3); S, alpha and theta_w values are not given in the text.

evidence.quote: calculated by analyzing the types of operations successfully executed by the agent and the quality of results.
evidence.support_explanation: Capability vector update delta-c is described only verbally; no formula for 'quality of results', no initial vectors, and Phi (task capability requirement) is produced by hand heuristics or LLM prompts that are not listed.

evidence.quote: The training set consists of 100 examples per type (total of 700 problems), while the test set consists of 20 examples per type (total of 140 problems).
evidence.support_explanation: Custom splits: MATH 700 train / 140 test; BBH 627 train / 100 test (5 per task, same 20 tasks); API-Bank 100 / 100 random sample (labels by GPT-4o-mini). Test sets are small and in-distribution with the evolution stream.

evidence.quote: The training set follows the MorphAgent setup, selecting 627 examples from 20 tasks. For testing, each task has 5 examples of varying difficulty, totaling 100 test problems.
evidence.support_explanation: BBH test: 100 problems from the same 20 tasks as training.

evidence.locator: Sec 4.4, Impact of Evolution Phase / Table 3
evidence.quote: On the MATH task, AgentNet achieves a score of 85.00 versus 77.86.
evidence.support_explanation: Evolution-on vs evolution-off (gpt-4o-mini, 3 agents), test split: MATH 77.86 to 85.00 (about 109 to 119 of 140), API-Bank 23.00 to 32.00, BBH 76.00 to 86.00. The ablation switches all evolution (memory, capability vectors, edge weights) at once; no per-component ablation and no definition of 'w/o evolution'.

evidence.quote: AgentNet consistently outperforms centralized frameworks such as MetaGPT
evidence.support_explanation: Headline comparison claim; see E009 for what Table 1 shows.

evidence.quote: Performance comparison of different methods across various tasks. In all multi-agent methods, we set
evidence.support_explanation: Table 1 (3 agents per multi-agent method, single run): DeepSeek-V3 AgentNet MATH 92.86 vs MetaGPT 92.14 / AFLOW 91.67 / Synapse 89.28 (1 problem of 140 is 0.71 point), BBH 94 vs 92, API-Bank 30 vs 29. GPT-4o-mini: MATH 85.00 tied with AFLOW and GPTSwarm, BBH 86 tied with GPTSwarm and above Self-Consistency 85, API-Bank 29 vs 24 React. Qwen-turbo: MATH 81.43 is below AFLOW 82.14 and Self-Refinement is 76.43; BBH 92 vs 75; API-Bank 32 vs 30. Our reading: the superiority claim holds on BBH and API-Bank, not uniformly on MATH.

evidence.quote: In our implementation, we configure the LLM API with a temperature of 0.0, a maximum token limit of 2048, and a top-p value of 1.0, ensuring consistent results throughout our experiments and enabling reliable comparisons and analysis.
evidence.support_explanation: Deterministic decoding means one run per cell and no sampling variance reported; Self-Consistency at temperature 0 is not explained. Baseline implementation details (whether baselines see the training set, call budgets) are not given.

evidence.quote: AgentNet achieves competitive or superior performance across all tasks.
evidence.support_explanation: Table 1 baseline levels look unstable: DeepSeek-V3 Direct 47.86 vs ReAct 77.14 vs Synapse 89.28 on MATH, MorphAgent 39.29 below Direct, with no explanation of answer extraction or scoring; the metric's sensitivity to prompt format is untested.

evidence.quote: However, with 5 agents, heterogeneous configurations outperform the homogeneous one, indicating that diversity enhances collaboration and complementary reasoning in larger teams.
evidence.support_explanation: Table 2 BBH (n=100): 3 agents 0.86/0.84/0.81/0.81, 5 agents 0.79/0.86/0.85/0.85. Differences of 1-7 points on 100 problems, single run; the inference about diversity is not statistically supported.

evidence.quote: Specifically, performance in the training phase increased from 80.38 for 3 agents and 30 executors to 81.18 for 9 agents and 40 executors.
evidence.support_explanation: Scalability evidence is AgentNet-only (training-phase BBH accuracy moves 0.8 points); no centralized baseline at scale, no latency, throughput or failure-injection experiment.

evidence.quote: As the number of agents increased, specialization became more evident, particularly in complex tasks, with certain agents excelling in specific areas while others focused on different abilities.
evidence.support_explanation: Specialisation is shown as agents' own ability scores after training; no test that specialised agents or routing by those scores cause the accuracy gain.

evidence.quote: AgentNet outperforms randomized methods, achieving 82.14% accuracy during training and 86.00% during testing.
evidence.support_explanation: Router ablation on BBH (random operations, random next agent, global router) is reported in a figure; the text gives numbers only for AgentNet. The 'Global Router' centralised comparison is the only direct test of the decentralisation claim and its values are not stated in text.

evidence.quote: While such designs simplify orchestration, they also introduce inherent constraints—including limited scalability, a single point of failure, and challenges to cross-organizational collaboration due to privacy and proprietary knowledge concerns.
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: centralized controllers and static roles. It is argued, not measured; compared baselines (AFLOW, GPTSwarm, MorphAgent) are offline-optimised designs rather than live central controllers.

evidence.quote: While these evolutionary approaches have shown promise, they primarily focus on individual agent adaptation rather than collective coordination.
evidence.support_explanation: Related-work claim against prompt/topology/role evolution (PromptBreeder, GPTSwarm, DyLAN, G-Designer, MorphAgent, AFlow, AgentSquare, EvoMAC); several of these already evolve topology at the collective level.

evidence.quote: Together, these design choices safeguard privacy and intellectual property, particularly crucial for cross-organizational collaborations.
evidence.support_explanation: Privacy and fault-tolerance benefits are asserted from design; no experiment on information exposure, agent failure, or cross-organisation setup appears in the paper.

evidence.quote: Experimental results demonstrate that AgentNet outperforms traditional centralized multi-agent systems, significantly improving efficiency, adaptability, and scalability in dynamic environments
evidence.support_explanation: Only accuracy is reported; no token, call, latency or evolution-phase cost measurement supports 'efficiency'.

evidence.quote: A trajectory-as-exemplar prompting method, which prompts the LLM with complete trajectories of the abstracted states and actions to improve multi-step decision-making.
evidence.support_explanation: Synapse is the closest memory-as-exemplar baseline; whether it received the same training trajectories and equal retrieval budget is not stated.

evidence.quote: Currently, the router selects agents from a relatively small pool of predefined candidates.
evidence.support_explanation: Stated limitation: routing is evaluated only with 3-9 predefined agents; exploration beyond the pool and heterogeneity at scale are future work.

signatures.object: Per-agent router memory M_rou and executor memory M_exe: fixed-capacity pools of (observation, partial context, action) fragments; baseline is the same agents without evolution.
signatures.information: Local steps in which the agent took part; a task-level success signal on the training split (definition not stated; labels exist for MATH, BBH, API-Bank); embeddings from bge-large-en-v1.5.
signatures.operation: On a successful training task, store the agent's own step fragments; on capacity, an LLM prompt decides the least useful fragment (frequency, recency, uniqueness) to drop; at a new task retrieve top-k by embedding similarity and inject as few-shot into reasoning and action prompts.
signatures.output: Retrieved fragments conditioning the router (forward/split/execute) and executor decisions.
signatures.conditions: Recurring task types; per-agent capacity C_max; k and C_max values not given in text.
signatures.feedback: Task success on the training split.
signatures.selection_rule: Admit successful fragments only; evict by LLM-judged utility. No marginal-gain test.
signatures.persistence: Per-agent in-memory pools across tasks; whether pools keep updating during the test phase is not stated.
signatures.later_use: Top-k retrieval at every later routing and execution step.
signatures.claimed_effect: Evolution on vs off (gpt-4o-mini, test split): MATH 77.86 to 85.00, API-Bank 23 to 32, BBH 76 to 86.
signatures.failure_boundary: Not reported: stale or harmful fragments, retrieval noise, memory size effects, store-only ablation.

signatures.object: Network state: directed edge weights w(i,j) and per-agent capability vectors c_i that drive entry-agent choice and forwarding/splitting targets.
signatures.information: Per-routed-pair success metric S and a per-task capability delta from an LLM-based assessment; task capability requirements from heuristics or LLM prompts.
signatures.operation: w <- alpha*w + (1-alpha)*S per interacting pair; edges below theta_w are removed; c <- beta*c + (1-beta)*delta-c; routing picks argmax capability-requirement similarity; DAG guaranteed by unchanged task state on forward.
signatures.output: Rewired topology and updated specialisation profile.
signatures.conditions: Predefined agent pool (3-9 agents); success metric defined per task.
signatures.persistence: Weights and capability vectors carried across tasks.
signatures.later_use: Entry-agent selection and routing at every later task.
signatures.claimed_effect: Autonomous specialisation (Fig 9) and network evolution (Fig 10); router better than random variants on BBH.
signatures.failure_boundary: No reversion if pruning removes a needed edge; no evidence specialisation causes accuracy gains.

gap.author_gap: Centralized or static-role multi-agent systems have scalability bottlenecks, single points of failure, limited adaptability, and block cross-organisation collaboration; prior evolutionary methods adapt individual agents or still use central control.
gap.checked_gap: Static roles and one-shot designs are real limitations, but the stated stakes (fault tolerance, privacy, scalability) are never measured. Compared neighbours (AFLOW, GPTSwarm, MorphAgent) are offline or profile-evolving designs, so the 'centralized controller' framing is only partly matched by the baselines.
gap.lineage: AutoGen/MetaGPT (static workflows) -> GPTSwarm/DyLAN/G-Designer (topology optimisation), AgentVerse/MorphAgent (role evolution), AFlow/AgentSquare (automated design), EvoMAC -> AgentNet adds per-agent retrieval memory and online weight/capability updates without a central router. Neighbours cited, not available as fixed local sources.
gap.closest_adjacent: GPTSwarm, MorphAgent, AFLOW, Synapse (trajectory exemplars) are in Table 1; DyLAN, G-Designer, AgentSquare are cited only.
gap.residue: Whether decentralisation, rather than memory or rerouting, accounts for any benefit; behaviour at hundreds of agents; exploration beyond predefined candidates (their stated limitation).
gap.method_response: Per-agent routers and memories, edge reweighting and capability vectors updated from task success, no central orchestrator.
gap.remaining_gap: No test of fault tolerance, privacy, or scale versus a centralized baseline except one figure-only router ablation; component contributions unseparated.
unresolved: Whether DyLAN/G-Designer-style online topology methods match AgentNet at equal cost could not be checked from fixed local sources.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: In a 3-agent gpt-4o-mini system, a training-phase evolution of per-agent retrieval memories, capability vectors and edge weights is associated with higher accuracy on small held-out in-distribution test sets of MATH, BBH and API-Bank (about +7, +10, +9 points, single run). AgentNet is competitive with, and on several cells tied with or below, strong multi-agent baselines. The decentralisation benefits (fault tolerance, privacy, scalability, efficiency) are not tested.
unresolved: Whether memory is frozen at test

G.reason: Static roles and one-shot designs are real limits and the evolutionary neighbours are listed, but the headline stakes (single point of failure, privacy, scalability) are not measured and the compared methods are not central controllers, so the nearest-neighbour comparison and residual bottleneck stay incomplete.

M.reason: Memory retrieval, EMA edge weights, capability vectors and forward/split/execute routing form a coherent mechanism, but key pieces (success metric S, delta-c, Phi, pruning prompt, hyperparameters) are verbal, and no distinguishable prediction separates decentralisation from plain memory plus routing.

X.reason: Algorithm 1 gives the loop, capacity-bounded pools with LLM-judged eviction, EMA decay and threshold pruning exist, but success definition, parameter values, test-time freezing, rollback and conflict handling are absent and the paper has no prompt appendix.

E.measurement.reason: Accuracy on custom 100-140 item splits with an undescribed scorer; baseline scores vary implausibly (DeepSeek-V3 Direct 47.86 vs Synapse 89.28 on MATH) and API-Bank categories are GPT-4o-mini labelled, so the metric's reliability is unverified.

E.causality.reason: An evolution-on/off test split result and a router ablation exist, but evolution is switched as one block, there is no memory-only, edge-only or capability-only control, no matched-budget or longer-context baseline, and the centralisation claim has only a figure-only global-router comparison.

E.holdout.reason: Disjoint train and test splits per benchmark are reported, but they are small and in-distribution (BBH test from the same 20 tasks), freezing at test is unstated, hyperparameter selection split is unknown, and no contamination or transfer test exists.

E.statistics.reason: Sample sizes are given and ties or losses are visible in Table 1, but all results are single deterministic runs with no intervals, and 1-problem margins and 1-7 point heterogeneity differences are read as effects.

E.cost.reason: The abstract claims improved efficiency, yet no token, call, latency, communication or evolution-phase cost is reported for AgentNet or baselines; baselines are matched only on number of agents.
